name: West International, runway 36L/18R
summary: The western of the test field's two parallel airliner runways, 1,310 m west of 36R. Landed on northward (36L) from its southern threshold; every end takes a 10 NM final.

sources.length_m: As Cape International's: the 747-400 at its maximum weight on a hot day, Boeing D6-58326-1 rev F 3.3.4, rounded up to 3,500 m.
sources.width_m: FAA AC 150/5300-13B change 1, table G-11 (C/D/E-V): 150 ft.
sources.protection: The same table as Cape International's, approach visibility below 3/4 mile; the test field's ground also keeps a 34:1 funnel clear 10 NM off each end (Airfield.pads_for).
sources.place: The test field's west side, x -18 km (lane/testfield step 0): a north-south runway so both of its 10 NM finals end at z +-20.3 km, inside the edge band at 24.5 km. An east-west one this far out could take no final from outside the map.
sources.parallel: FAA Order JO 7110.65 5-9-7: simultaneous independent ILS approaches to parallel runways 4,300 ft (1,310 m) apart or more.
sources.pattern: The outer side at each end (AC 90-66C 11.1): landing north on 36L the pattern is to the west, the left; landing south on 18R it is to the west, the right.
